Total number of questions — 20
76
Eco Mark certification
*241. SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) the number of products that have
been identified for Eco Mark since 1991;
(b) the basis on which such Eco Mark
certification is given; and
(c) the steps taken to popularise the
Eco Mark among producers and customers?
Vanishing brides and abandoned
grooms abroad
*242. MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA: Will the
Minister of OVERSEAS INDIAN
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the number
of cases of vanishing brides and abandoned
grooms abroad has increased in the recent
past;
(b) whether Government had formed a
Committee in this regard; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
 National policy for protection of rivers
†*243. SHRI PYARELAL
KHANDELWAL: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that water of
most of the major rivers has become black
after getting polluted;
(b) whether it is also a fact that all efforts
to deal with the said problem have proved
infructuous;
(c) if so, whether Government are
considering to formulate any national policy
to protect rivers from getting polluted; and
(d) if not, the details thereof, State-
wise?
Melting of ice in upper region of Tibet
†*244. SHRI JANESHWAR
MISHRA:
SHRI BRIJ BHUSHAN
TIWARI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that rapid melting
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

77
of ice in upper region of Tibet, shrinking of
glaciers, grass turning yellow and drying of
rivers have posed a serious danger to the
environment;
(b) if so, whether Government have
conducted any study with regard to its
adverse effects on the country; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Upgradation of services by DoP
*245. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether in view of the burgeoning
competition from private courier
companies, the Department of Posts has
embarked upon a major strategy to rejig its
operations across the country and has
worked out a four-pronged strategy to
consolidate its position;
(b) if so, the main strategies formulated;
(c) to what extent it would be helpful;
and
(d) whether Government are also
considering to upgrade traditional services
through induction of technology,
introduction of new products and services
to meet the challenges of faster, more
reliable and more responsive services to
customers?
Accident database
*246. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Sundar Committee
Report on Road Safety and Traffic
Management had commented that data on
road accidents injuries and mortality was
both inadequate and scattered;
(b) whether the United Nation's
Economic and Social Commission for Asia
and the Pacific (UNESCAP) has come
forward to fund a project to build an accident
database; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Colachal Port
*247. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the
Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a joint venture
agreement was entered into for
development of Colachal Port with Klana
Port of Malaysia;
(b) if so, the major terms of agreement
and the time-frame before which the project
is to be completed;
(c) the present stage and progress of
the project;
(d) whether there are any constraints in
the completion of the project;
(e) if so, the measures envisaged to get
over such problems; and
(f) the initiatives taken to develop the
minor ports in Tamil Nadu?
Boundary talks with China
*248. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: W ill the Minister of
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether boundary talks between
India and China had made significant
progress and the border areas remained
peaceful and tranquil and whether this issue
was discussed with the Chinese President
during his recent visit to India;

78
(b) if so, the other issues that were
discussed;
(c) whether any final agreement on the
boundary issue was signed; and
(d) if so, the latest position thereon?
New CZM Notification
*249. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
SHRI D. RAJA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have made a new Coastal Zone
Management (CZM) Notification replacing
the Coastal

Total number of questions — 155
423
Development of technique for
preservation of fruits
1829. SHRIMATI VIPLOVE
THAKUR: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Bhaba Atomic
Research Centre (BARC) has developed a
technique of long lasting preservation of
fruits;
(b) if so, whether this technique has
been adopted for preservation of various
types of fruits and vegetables in Himachal
Pradesh;
(c) if so, the results thereof, and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Shortage of coal washeries
†1830. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA : Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether there is shortage of coal
washeries in the country;
(b) whether Government propose to
enhance the number of coal washeries
keeping in view the introduction of clean
coal technology;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether Government propose to
make it mandatory for captive coal mines
to build washeries; and
(e) if so, by when the directions would
be issued in this regard?
Formation of a Regulatory
Commission
†1831. SHRI LAXMINARAYAN
SHARMA: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state by when the action
regarding formation of a Regulatory
Commission would be taken for proper
control over the rates, supply of coal and
its quality?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

424
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Losses incurred by CIL
†1832. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) the number of coal mines of Coal
India Ltd. (CIL) which are running in losses
at present;
(b) the amount of loss incurred to the
company every year as a result of mines
running in losses; and
(c) the action being taken to improve
the condition of these mines?
Allotment of coal fields
†1833. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that 745
applications have been received for the
allotment of 15 coal fields in the country;
(b) if not, the facts in this regard;
(c) whether petitioners include those
people also to whom coal fields have been
allotted for mining earlier;
(d) if so, the names of those people and
names of the people out of them who have
not made any production as per rule in the
allotted coal fields so far; and
(e) whether Government would
blacklist such petitioners of these coal
fields?
Waterlogging in coal mines of
Madhya Pradesh
†1834. MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the danger that may arise out of water-
logging in underground coal mines of Tansi,
Chhindwada of Madhya Pradesh;
(b) whether one section of this mine
closed down totally or partially in the
month of April;
(c) if so, the steps taken or being taken
to overcome the danger arisen out of water-
logging; and
(d) the details of safety measures taken
in this mine for future?
Security threat for coal companies
1835. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is
security threat for coal companies in our
country; and
(b) if so, the actions taken by
Government to provide proper security
systems for those companies?
Setting up of coal washeries
1836. SHRI B.J. P ANDA : W ill the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Centre has directed the
CIL and its subsidiaries to push up setting
up of coal washeries or expanding the
existing ones to boost supply of coal;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) to what extent this would help meet
the needs of the consumers?
Review of private sector ownership of
coal mines
1837. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT :
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that all coal mines

are owned by public sector, private sector
and joint sector;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
(c) whether Government are considering
review of private sector ownership of coal
mines;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?

Will the Minister of COMMUNI-

credit card companies engaging recovery
agents, the telecom operators have also
employed recovery agents, who intimidate
subscribers for paying up their due
